value.strategy: The returns were primarily driven by i) reinvestment of maturity proceeds into a much more favourable spread environment and, ii) the portfolio benefiting from spread tightening at certain points in the period. As one would expect from such an active year, there were a significant number of changes to the underlying holdings in the portfolio. Throughout 2023 and into 2024, we continued to reduce our exposure to Florida Hurricane risk. All this was achieved while reducing the expected loss of the fund and keeping portfolio spreads generally at, or above 1000bps.
value.selection_process: The selection process involves reinvestment of maturity proceeds into a much more favourable spread environment, benefiting from spread tightening, and making significant changes to underlying holdings. Specifically, throughout 2023 and into 2024, the fund continued to reduce its exposure to Florida Hurricane risk, while keeping portfolio spreads generally at, or above 1000bps.
value.asset_types: The fund invests in insurance-linked securities (ILS) and the reinsurance market, primarily catastrophe bonds. By risk contribution, Florida Hurricane remains the dominant exposure, with Texas Hurricane as the second biggest exposure.
value.real_objectives: The real objectives include reducing the expected loss of the fund and keeping portfolio spreads generally at, or above 1000bps.
value.fund_history: Over the last few years, the risk profile of the portfolio had been fairly stable. By risk contribution, Florida Hurricane remains the dominant exposure of the fund, while Texas Hurricane took over from California Earthquake as the second biggest exposure.
